name: Joomla Login Brute Force
execution: wfuzz -w $WORDLIST -d "username=fuzz&password=$PASS" $TARGET/administrator/index.php
wfuzz -w $WORDLIST -d "username=fuzz&password=$PASS&secret_token=FUZZ" $TARGET/administrator/index.php
wfuzz -w $WORDLIST -d "username=fuzz&password=$PASS" -b "$COOKIE" $TARGET/administrator/index.php

decision_points.then: Attempt brute force login with common usernames and a guessed password derived from reconnaissance.

success_indicators: Successful login to Joomla administrator panel

name: Joomla Admin Shell Upload
execution: Navigate to Extensions -> Templates -> [Selected Template]
Create a new file (e.g., 'shell.php')
Upload PHP code with a system command execution payload (e.g., '<?php system("whoami"); ?>')
Access the uploaded shell via URL (e.g., $TARGET/templates/[TemplateName]/shell.php)

decision_points.then: Upload a PHP shell via the template editor for code execution.

name: Joomla Reverse Shell
execution: Upload a PHP script to the web server (e.g., using template editor).
The PHP script executes a bash reverse shell command.
Listen for incoming connection on $LHOST:$LPORT using netcat.
Trigger the PHP script via a web request to execute the reverse shell.

decision_points.if: Code execution achieved on Joomla server
decision_points.then: Upload and trigger a PHP script to establish a reverse shell.

name: TTY Upgrade
execution: Send the shell to background (Ctrl+Z).
Execute 'stty raw -echo'.
Bring the shell to foreground (fg).
Press Enter to complete TTY upgrade.

decision_points.then: Attempt to upgrade the shell to a fully interactive TTY session.

success_indicators: Interactive shell with full TTY capabilities (arrow keys, tab completion)

name: Read User Flag
execution: Navigate to the user's home directory.
Attempt to read the 'user.txt' file.

decision_points.if: Interactive shell access and user home directory accessible
decision_points.then: Attempt to read the 'user.txt' flag file.

name: Read Password Backup File
execution: Navigate to the directory containing the password backup file.
Display the contents of the 'password_backup' file.

decision_points.if: Interactive shell access and a potential password backup file is found
decision_points.then: Display the contents of the password backup file to examine its format.

success_indicators: Hex dump or encoded data displayed from password backup file

name: Hex Dump Decryption

indicators: hex dump content from password backup

execution: Use 'xxd -r' to reverse the hex dump.
Use 'file' to identify the archive type.
Decompress archives using appropriate tools (e.g., 'bzcat', 'zcat', 'tar xf').

decision_points.if: Password backup file contains hex dump data
decision_points.then: Attempt to reverse the hex dump and identify/decompress any nested archives to reveal the password.

name: SSH Login with Found Credentials
execution: ssh $USER@$TARGET

decision_points.if: Username and password for a user are discovered
decision_points.then: Attempt to SSH into the target machine using the discovered credentials.

name: Joomla Admin Area Reconnaissance
execution: Navigate to the admin area directory (e.g., /var/www/html/administrator).
List files and directories within the admin area.
Examine file permissions and modification times.

decision_points.then: Explore the Joomla admin area directory for interesting files and configurations.

success_indicators: Discovery of files like 'input' and 'report' within the admin area

name: Input File Manipulation
execution: Modify the 'input' file with a target URL or command.
Monitor the 'report' file for changes or output.
Use 'curl' to fetch content from a controlled web server.
Write fetched content to the 'input' file.

decision_points.then: Manipulate the 'input' file to influence the 'report' file and observe the results.

success_indicators: Changes in 'report' file content based on 'input' file modifications
Execution of commands via 'input' file manipulation
follow_up: Read Root Flag via Cron Job

name: Read Root Flag via Cron Job
execution: Identify a cron job that processes the 'input' file.
Craft a malicious 'input' file content to fetch a 'sudoers' file.
Place a modified 'sudoers' file on a controlled web server.
Trigger the cron job by modifying the 'input' file.
Use 'sudo' with the modified 'sudoers' file to gain root privileges.

decision_points.if: A cron job is found to be processing an 'input' file
decision_points.then: Exploit the cron job by manipulating the 'input' file to achieve privilege escalation.

name: Root Shell
execution: Execute 'sudo su' or equivalent command to gain a root shell.

name: Read Root Flag
execution: Navigate to the root directory.
Read the 'root.txt' file.

name: Pspy Process Monitoring
execution: Download 'pspy' binary.
Make 'pspy' executable.
Run 'pspy' to monitor running processes and file system events.

decision_points.then: Utilize 'pspy' to monitor system processes and identify potential attack vectors or scheduled tasks.

success_indicators: Discovery of scheduled tasks or interesting process activity

name: Identify Cron Job Execution
execution: Observe 'pspy' output for cron job executions.
Identify the commands being executed by cron jobs.

decision_points.then: Identify the specific commands and timing of cron job executions.

success_indicators: Identification of specific cron job commands and their execution

name: Exploit Cron Job Command
execution: Analyze the identified cron job command for vulnerabilities.
Craft malicious input to be processed by the cron job.
Use 'curl' to fetch malicious content to the target server.
Modify files that are processed by the cron job to achieve privilege escalation.

decision_points.if: A cron job command is identified
decision_points.then: Exploit the command executed by the cron job to gain higher privileges.

success_indicators: Privilege escalation achieved through cron job exploitation
